feeds_accelerator_ids.note: Start = the completion of the Booster (1991); the AGS is the next machine in the chain, for RHIC and (earlier and still) for the AGS programme.
feeds_accelerator_ids.quote: The Booster then feeds the beam into the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron.

intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: Construction of the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron (AGS) Booster was begun in 1986 and completed in 1991.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: Start = completion year; the Booster is described in the present tense (it feeds the AGS and the NASA Space Radiation Laboratory) on the pages read on 2026-10-26.
intervals.quote: Construction of the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron (AGS) Booster was begun in 1986 and completed in 1991.

name: AGS Booster
notes: Source of the energetic heavy-ion beams of the NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) as well as the AGS injector; NSRL has no record in the Atlas.

Kinetic energy: the 1.5 GeV is for protons; the heavy-ion energy at Booster extraction is lower per nucleon and is not recorded. A 2023 RHIC review gives "2.3 GeV" for the same stage, apparently a total (not kinetic) energy; the kinetic figure of the Reviews of Modern Physics article is used.

beam_energy.locator: Aidala et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 85, 655 (arXiv:1209.2803), §II.A
beam_energy.note: Protons, after injection at 200 MeV from the Linac.
beam_energy.quote: In the case of polarized-proton running at RHIC, a pulse of polarized H− ions from the source is accelerated to 200 MeV in the linac, then stripped of its electrons as it is injected and captured as a single bunch of polarized protons in the Booster, which accelerates the protons to 1.5 GeV.

injection_energy.quote: accepting heavy ions from EBIS or protons from the 200-million electron volt (MeV) Linac.

summary.plain: A small ring, a quarter the size of the AGS, built in 1986-1991 to give protons and heavy ions a first push before they enter the AGS. It lifts protons from 200 million to 1.5 billion electronvolts.
summary.technical: Rapid-cycling booster synchrotron (Building 942) accepting 200 MeV H- ions from the Linac (stripped on injection) or heavy ions from EBIS, accelerating protons to 1.5 GeV kinetic energy for the AGS; also the heavy-ion source for NSRL.
